**Delegated-review requests.** `pose review request <scope|bundle> --kind delegated-review [--purpose review|adjudicate|smoke] [--agents <name,...>] [--note-file <path>] [--apply]` opens an action request of kind `delegated-review` that binds the project, the worktree, the scope, the sealed bundle, the brief, the notes, the policies, the accepted agents and the destination of the conclusion (an attestation, an adjudication record or smoke evidence). No actor answers it: `pose action fulfil <act-id> --run <run-id> --runner agent:<id> --idempotency-key <key> --expected-revision <n> [--channel cli|ci|conductor] [--envelope <file>] [--apply]`, or the MCP tool `pose_action_fulfil`, submits a completed run, and the engine records the fulfilment only when the run is of the request's brief and bundle, of an accepted agent, completed with its containment, its signed proof verifies, its attempt ledger is intact and the engine recorded its conclusion at the request's destination; the fulfilment is verified again on every read. `pose delegate review <scope> --request <act-id>` runs the request's brief locally and submits the run once concluded. A rejecting run fulfils the request without approving anything; a superseded bundle or changed policy invalidates it, even once fulfilled, and it is asked again with `--supersedes <act-id>`, which retires it under the supersession authority rules (`--authority <json>`, `--role <role>`, `--requested-at` from the preview), or, when the plan now reserves the review for a person, makes the person's escalation its successor; a retry with the same key and run is a no-op. A person is asked by exception, as a decision request to the maintainer role: a plan that reserves the review for a person, a spent attempt budget, reviewers in conflict, and a `business_decision` a reviewer raised in its draft. A run's proof verifies in any checkout of the project: the worktree it ran in is recorded, not required of the reader, so a CI job or the Conductor fulfils the request with the same envelope.

Opt in to the verification bar with `delegated_review: true` in review policy only when preparing adoption. This live bar requires a signed run reference for agent different-actor review and refuses a prefix-only identity; it does not enable or add the future catalog capability. Non-adopting instances keep declared behavior. Under explicit executor-attested trust, normalized vendor OR model difference satisfies different-actor (vendor difference preferred); unknown baselines and the same vendor/model refuse. A machine run never satisfies mandatory-human. Catalog adoption, cutoffs/rollback and automatic conclusion application remain separate capability work.

Read the same current assurance through verify, review-check, MCP and `pose state --attention`: `machine-attested` names the signed executor declaration, its source, run/proof and vendor/model comparisons. Current issuer pins, project/audience/time, sealed inputs, retained artifacts and original/continuation receipts are reverified. Revocation, missing receipts, rewritten data or stale inputs remove machine assurance. Signing does not reset quotas or erase earlier rejecting runs. The origin worktree is recorded with the run, not required of the reader: a proof verifies in any checkout of the project, so a run a CI job or the Conductor performed is verified like a local one; no universal containment is claimed.

…  from another process, or
  from before a restart, fails the signature and the caller restarts from the
  first page. No daemon and no resident state: a one-shot CLI needs no cursor.
- **Continuation:** the collection is recomputed and its digest compared; a
  changed collection, generation, tool, project or filter set is refused with a
  `cursor-*` code (`cursor-stale`, `cursor-binding`, `cursor-signature`,
  `cursor-expired`, `cursor-position`, `cursor-unsupported-version`,
  `cursor-malformed`). It never continues over a changed collection and never
  restarts silently at page zero. Version 1 tokens are refused as unsupported,
  not reinterpreted.
- **Query binding:** the project and the canonical filters are digested into the
  token, so its size does not depend on the filters; equivalent filters (lists
  trimmed, case-folded, de-duplicated and sorted, then encoded as JSON so that no
  delimiter inside a value makes two queries read alike; `recent` implies date
  ordering; an omitted `sort` is `slug`, the listing's default order) bind the
  same cursor.
- **Generation and race:** the index generation is read before the collection
  and again before the page is labelled; a publication in between refuses the
  call (retry) instead of mislabelling items, and the generation status, reason
  and the legacy files that diverge from it are disclosed. Verifying a
  generation reads and hashes every index file (tens of megabytes on this
  corpus), so the verification is reused per project while the descriptor and
  the files it names, with their legacy counterparts, keep the same size, mode
  and modification time, plus the inode and status-change time on Linux (an
  edit that restores size and mtime still moves them) and, for a link, the same
  target and target metadata; a page after the first reads only the collection.
- **Bounds:** a token is at most 2048 bytes (checked on issue as well as on
  receipt) and lives 15 minutes; a page is at most 500 items (a larger `limit`
  is clamped and the clamp is disclosed), and a continuation without `limit` is
  still a bounded page.
- **Disclosure:** every page carries its generation, collection digest,
  position, total and a statement that it is a navigation view of a collection
  read for the call: an absent `next_cursor` means that collection was
  exhausted, not that nothing is pending elsewhere, and a page authorizes no
  gate or effect (those read current inputs).
- **Compatibility:** only a call that names neither cursor nor limit returns
  everything, as before. `limit` without a cursor starts a paginated walk.
- **Arguments:** `limit` and `cursor` are read from the exact names only; a
  differently-cased alias, a null `cursor` and a null, zero or negative `limit`
  are refused on every paginated tool, so the call that returns everything is only the call that names
  neither.
- **Cost:** every page states its cost: these tools load their whole
  collection, so each page recomputes it and its exact total (`cost:
  full-scan`); `limit` bounds the page returned, not the work done.

## Consequences

- No duplicated or skipped item between pages: either the same collection or an
  explicit restart. The cost of a page is one recomputation of the collection,
  which every call already paid; the page is cut after the domain layer orders
  and filters.
- A cursor never outlives a server restart. That is deliberate and disclosed.
- The total is the size of the recomputed collection and costs a full scan for
  these list tools, which load their whole collection; the cost is stated, not
  hidden behind an optimization that does not exist.
- Adding a paginated tool means calling the shared helper with the tool's
  filters and keys.

Rejected: retaining a snapshot per cursor (unbounded memory, a daemon the CLI
does not have); an unsigned token with a generation field (trivially forged,
replayable across queries); keying the collection by offset alone (cannot tell
a reordering from the same collection); a durable key on disk (a secret in the
repository tree for little gain over a restart).

# Rule: Knowledge Governance

## When to consult

Consult this guide when creating, updating, reviewing, or removing artifacts under `.pose/knowledge/`.

## TTL and retention

- Set `expires_at` on every artifact when it is created.
- Use a default TTL of 30 days for notes, decision logs, and handoffs.
- Use a TTL of up to 90 days only with a justification recorded in the artifact body.
- Treat an artifact without `expires_at` as non-compliant and block its creation or merge.

## When this is not the right home

- Use `.pose/knowledge/` only for time-bound operational memory: content
  tied to a decision moment, a handoff between executions, or something
  meant to be reviewed and eventually expire.
- A durable fact or convention that will not become false and carries no
  review trigger — a third-party tool's parsing quirk, a naming
  convention, a recurring gotcha — is not a `decision-log` just because no
  better type exists. Route it to `.pose/rules/` instead: add it to an
  existing rule file or create one, then wire it into the relevant task
  type's base `rules` array in `.pose/indexes/task-map.json` so
  `pose suggest <task>` surfaces it automatically. No path scoping is
  required — a task type's base `rules` list is returned regardless of
  `--path`; only language/component-specific rules need the
  `rules_by_domain` layer.
- Rule of thumb: if nothing was decided or traded off, and nothing about
  the fact will change on a predictable timeline, it is not a
  `decision-log` and not an ADR — it is a rule. See ADR
  `2026-08-15-durable-non-architectural-knowledge-belongs-in-rules-not-a-new-type`.

## Reusable cross-execution format

- Structure reusable context as a handoff with fixed sections: Context, Current state, Next checks, Risks, and Next owner.
- Keep `source_refs` linked to the relevant spec, workflow, and executed check commands.
- Record `last_reviewed_at` in the body to make effective cross-execution updates traceable.

## Archiving and purging

- Run biweekly triage to list expired artifacts.
- Move expired artifacts to `.pose/knowledge/archive/` when they retain audit value.
- Purge archived artifacts 180 days after expiration unless documented legal or compliance requirements apply.
- Record every archive and purge action in the housekeeping log.

## Sensitive content

- Prohibit secrets, tokens, credentials, private keys, and equivalent material.
- Prohibit personal data and non-anonymized customer data.
- Do not copy restricted incidents or reports in full; keep only a controlled reference.
- Classify frontmatter `sensitivity` as `public-internal` or `restricted`.
- Remove identified sensitive content immediately and open a security follow-up.

## Ownership and review

- Keep `@pose-maintainers` as the primary governance owner.
- Require an owner in every artifact frontmatter.
- Review expiration biweekly and quality monthly.
- Escalate a backlog overdue by more than two cycles to the primary owner.
- Block backlog growth when `list-expired` exceeds the operational limit: zero in strict mode, two in tolerant mode.

## Minimum operational checks

- Run `pose knowledge-check --strict` biweekly to validate the expired backlog.
- Run `pose knowledge-housekeeping list-expired` for detailed triage.
- Run `pose knowledge-housekeeping archive-expired --dry-run` before applying changes.
- Execute destructive actions only with an explicit `--apply` flag.

+### Keep delegated work proportional
+
+Delegate a bounded question or change with named paths, acceptance criteria,
+allowed access and a stopping condition. Give the worker relevant references
+and excerpts; keep full transcripts and command output in files. Use the native
+`task` purpose for implementation or investigation and the generated sealed brief
+for governed review, adjudication or smoke conclusions.
+
+- Keep coordination and mechanical CLI steps with the primary execution. Do not
+  add a secondary coordinator merely to watch another worker or fill CLI forms.
+- Inspect `agents` and preview the route once before starting. Record the chosen
+  model, vendor, effort, access and attempt; preserve the independence required
+  by the sealed plan.
+- Use native `watch` or `wait` to follow a run. Report stage changes and findings;
+  do not spend agent turns repeatedly reading unchanged logs.
+- Resume or hand off the existing attempt when its state permits. Preserve failed
+  and quota-limited records and respect their budgets. Do not start a fresh run
+  to bypass a limit or invent a reset time the provider did not report.
+- Before a detached review of a new scope, ensure the sealed checkout contains
+  matching indexed attribution and structured validation for its source. Persist
+  missing derived inputs before final validation; uncommitted results and indexes
+  are unavailable in that checkout.
+- Check provider authentication and output/capture framing when configuring an
+  agent or after a setup failure. Availability and a routing preview do not prove
+  a successful model request or a verifiable conclusion.
+- Run focused regressions while changing code. Reuse current canonical evidence
+  when native coverage and provenance support it, and repeat checks invalidated
+  by a material change. Preserve required checks, controls and independent
+  judgments; a task's success is not review approval.
+- Reuse applicable corpus and fixtures. Add an extra experiment only for an
+  identified risk, contract or finding, with a bounded scope. Qualification of a
+  separate engine-wide pilot is not an automatic checklist for every spec.
+- Track machine time and CPU/RAM separately from model input/output and cached
+  tokens. Do not infer billed cost or unique context from cumulative token counts.
+
+Use these practices within the existing review plan and task workflow. They do
+not create another mandatory rehearsal, report or approval layer. Keep the
+technical details of execution routing in the sections below.

 ### Bound delegated adapter execution
 
 Declare an optional `containment` object on each agent in `.pose/policy/delegation.json`. Use containment schema 1 and `trusted-process`. This backend runs a trusted local executable; a disposable worktree shares Git metadata and does not isolate filesystem, original repository, network, credential files, CPU or memory. Required guarantees that the host cannot enforce are refused before reserving an attempt or spawning a process. Linux process-group termination requires an observable process inventory and is checked after kill; descendants that escape the group remain outside its coverage. Windows/other ports do not qualify group containment from a cross-build.

## Risks

- Não converter controles positivos de `current` em `unknown` para esconder
  falhas; tampouco promover índice legado ou prova histórica a autorização atual.
- Preservar o contrato de verificação histórica: metadado atual desconhecido
  não equivale automaticamente à invalidação de uma aprovação histórica;
  autoridade, trust e fontes necessárias ilegíveis ou revogadas continuam
  bloqueando o que seu contrato exigir.
- Um diretório comprovadamente sem Git pode sustentar um build de índices
  exclusivamente de filesystem; inputs materiais de refs/histórico continuam
  exigindo a prova Git correspondente.
- Limites recalibrados em D6: 25.000 registros agregados, 512 MiB de inputs,
  8 MiB de metadados, 16 roots, profundidade federada oito e uma repetição.
  D5 conserva 64 arestas de dependência e 256 identidades/entradas por grafo/lista.
  A calibração reteve 18.905 registros e cerca de 353,5 MiB em memória; não publicou
  índices e não equivale aos gates normais. Nenhum truncamento certifica completude.
- Writers externos e uma edição A→B→A que desaparece antes da auditoria não
  recebem garantia transacional. O fencing só cobre participantes do protocolo.
- O assessment de dívida lido nesta tarefa foi incompleto: duas specs históricas
  inválidas não puderam ser lidas. Não reportar esse scan como completo.
